deviations: F2 — the lane's vector is refuted; the fix stands on a measured one. The lane wrote that an unguarded native.return?.() would displace "the caller's own error thrown from the for...of body". Measurement refutes that: ECMAScript IteratorClose returns the original completion when the caller is already throwing, so a return-fault is discarded by the language on that path — under a planted finally fault the caller-throw case stayed green while the break, early-return and normal-completion cases reddened. The reachable escape is the opposite path. I re-aimed the instrument at `break` after db.close() and reproduced the defect with a real vector, no plant: 'expected NOT_SQLITE_ERROR to be NO_THROW', a raw non-SQLiteError escaping the caller's for...of. Guard applied on that evidence; the code comment names the measured vector, not the stated one.

F2's blast radius reached prose the lane did not name. Swallowing the finalize fault makes guides/sqlite.md Contract item 5 ("Every native node:sqlite throw is mapped at the boundary to a SQLiteError") and the SQLiteStatementInterface @remarks ("A native fault surfaces as a SQLiteError") false in that corner. .claude/rules/documentation.md § Parity requires correcting drift in the same change, so both now name finalizing as the exception; guides/sqlite.md:281 and the SQLiteStatement.test.ts header comment, which enumerate that file's subjects, gained the new case.

F1 — the lane's prescription was adopted verbatim ("on every exit after the first step"), and the rest of the sentence left alone. The F2 fix then required a further sentence in the same comment naming why the call is guarded, which the lane did not write. I wrote it and held it to what was measured ("Finalizing can itself fault") rather than asserting it always faults — writing a stronger claim would have reintroduced exactly F1's defect class.

Observation outside the rows, for the capability that owns it: a never-stepped iterate() result finalizes nothing — the generator body never runs, so neither the finally nor native.return?.() is reached. Nothing leaks today because the eager native iterator holds no read transaction until it is stepped. Closing it would mean finalizing on a path the generator protocol does not run, which is a design decision outside the ruled repair.
